To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the symptoms of asthma are due to an abnormality in the response of the ASM to inflammation, that this abnormality is due to mast cell infiltration of ASM and that the symptoms of bronchiectasis are due to inflammation localized to the epithelial lining of the airways.
the features that distinguish asthma from bronchitis are due to abnormalities of airway smooth muscle responsiveness and that these abnormalities are due to mast cell myosistis.

(i) asthma is a disease characterized by variable airflow limitation and AHR; (ii) the inflammation in asthma is eosinophilic, but there are other inflammatory conditions, such as allergic rhinitis and eosinophilic airway inflammation, which are not associated with asthma; (iii) the inflammation in eosinophilic asthma is associated with infiltration of ASM by mast cells and this may account for the variable airflow obstruction; (iv) airway inflammation may lead to AHR
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between inflammation in the airway and the symptoms of asthma and the mechanisms by which inflammation causes these symptoms.
the mechanisms of airway inflammation and the role it plays in the pathogenesis of airway hyperresponsiveness and airway obstruction.
understanding the relationship between airways inflammation and asthma and how this relationship is modified by other factors such as infection and allergen exposure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
asthma is a condition in which there is airway inflammation, usually eosinophilic, that results in variable airflow obstruction and AHR, but this statement would not be very informative.
inflammation is a necessary but not sufficient cause of asthma.
the pathogenesis of airway hyper-resistance (AHR) is due to an abnormality in the responsiveness of ASM to inflammatory mediators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asthma is a disease of the ASM, with inflammation being only one of the many factors that contribute to its development.
the pathogenesis of bronchitis is the result of Th2-mediated inflammation of the epithelium, and the pathogenesis of airway obstruction is the result of mast cell myosistis of ASM.
asthma is caused by a Th2-mediated myositis of the ASM, and that inflammation of the epithelium, lamina propria and submucosa is only relevant in so far as it leads to this condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
asthma is a condition in which airway inflammation, which may be of many different types, results in abnormalities in smooth muscle function.
inflammation, at least eosinophilic inflammation, is not a cause of asthma but is a response to it, and that the features of asthma (obstruction and AHR) are due to abnormalities of ASM.

asthma is not a single disease, but a collection of diseases with different pathophysiological mechanisms, and that inflammation, while a feature of some forms of asthma, is not the cause of all forms of asthma.
